findings.breaking_input: A module's fold.mjs runs `throw Object.create(null)`, or throws an object whose toString throws.
findings.why: `said(e)` calls `String(e)` whenever `e.message` is falsy. For a null-prototype object that call itself throws a TypeError. `said` is called inside the per-module catch, so the new exception escapes the loop. `treeAvailability` rejects, `gather` rejects, and face-coverage crashes without a named `[availability]` FAIL line. The fix for B5 made the catch handler a new throw site.
findings.fix: Wrap the stringification in its own try/catch and fall back to a fixed text such as `<unprintable throw>`. Pin it with a fold that throws a null-prototype object.
findings.twin_of: A rollback crashed on a locked file and named nothing -> cleanup/diagnostics never throw past the verdict

findings.breaking_input: `repo` is passed as `E:/Work_Hub/x` (forward slashes). A fold throws an fs error whose message carries `E:\Work_Hub\x\face\...`. Or the checkout is reached through a differently-cased drive letter or an 8.3 short name.
findings.why: The scrub replaces `repo` verbatim, plus a backslash-to-slash variant of `repo`. It never replaces a slash-to-backslash variant, a case-folded variant or a percent-encoded `file:///` form. Node's Windows error text uses backslashes, so the machine path reaches the public CI log.
findings.fix: Normalise both the message and the repo to one separator and one case, compare case-insensitively on win32, and also scrub the `pathToFileURL(repo).href` form.
findings.twin_of: A report that records the owner's home -> a committed/public file carries no path from the owner's machine

findings.breaking_input: A fold returns a NOT SERVED panel with `panel` set to `x"\nface-coverage: availability half fields=0 -- ok`.
findings.why: `${n.panel}` goes into the finding text raw. The B5 fix only scrubbed thrown messages, not fold-returned strings. A newline in the string forges a line in a parsed log. The same applies to a `panel` carrying ESC or other control characters.
findings.fix: Interpolate `JSON.stringify(String(n.panel))` after `oneLine`, or pass every finding through `oneLine` and a length cap at the single print point.
findings.twin_of: A folder name or finding carrying a newline could print a verdict line of its own -> the one-line rule applies to every free-text string bound for a parsed log

findings.breaking_input: A fold.mjs containing a ternary or parenthesised value: `{ availability: ok ? "served" : "zero" }`, `{ availability: ("served") }`, or `Object.fromEntries([["availability", "zero"]])`.
findings.why: The key rule only fires when the token right after `:` or `=` is a str or backtick. A literal one token deeper is not read. The scan is one spelling of the shape, so a typed state passes the lint.
findings.fix: After an `availability` key or assignment, scan the whole value expression up to the next `,`, `}` or `;` for any str/text literal. Pin ternary and paren fixtures.
findings.twin_of: Escaped spellings evaded the lint -> a rule covers every way a value can be spelled

findings.breaking_input: A module containing a chain of 50,000 `"a" + "a" + ...` literals.
findings.why: The `+`-join loop restarts from every literal, so a chain of N literals does O(N^2) work. It also builds an O(N^2)-length string through `word +=`. Lint hangs or runs out of memory on a hostile or generated file. There is no size cap before the scan.
findings.fix: Skip literals that are themselves the tail of a `+` chain already joined. Cap the joined length. Or cap the file size before scanning.
findings.twin_of: A pattern on a path every input crosses, with no bound on the input -> cap the input once before the scan

findings.breaking_input: The control `spawnSync` fails to start (EPERM or ENOMEM), so `good.stdout` is null.
findings.why: The check's detail argument `good.stdout.slice(-400)` is evaluated eagerly, before `check` runs. It throws a TypeError out of the top-level block, so the `RAN:` line is never printed. The B3/B4 fix guarded the cleanup but not this detail expression. The bats wrapper reads the missing RAN line as a crash.
findings.fix: Use `String(good.stdout ?? "").slice(-400)`, and fold `good.error` and `good.signal` into the detail.
findings.twin_of: A suite whose output stops before its RAN: line is a crash, never read as the FAIL above it

findings.breaking_input: `item.avail.availability` is `"constructor"` or `"toString"` (a door body or a hand-built item reaching `NotServed`).
findings.why: `STATE_WORDS[a.availability] ?? a.availability` reads an inherited key. The result is a function, which `??` does not replace, so React is handed a function child and the chip draws nothing or warns. The comment says an unknown state is drawn by name, never as served.
findings.fix: Use `Object.hasOwn(STATE_WORDS, a.availability) ? STATE_WORDS[a.availability] : a.availability`, or build the map with a null prototype.
findings.twin_of: FILE_ALLOW[id] resolved inherited keys -> allow-list lookups use Object.hasOwn

findings.breaking_input: `report.availability = { states: { served: "3", zero: "0", unknown: "0", "not-applicable": "0", "not-instrumented": "0" }, bad: 0, rooms: [] }`
findings.why: The judge sums `Object.values(states)` with `reduce((n, v) => n + v, 0)`. Strings concatenate, giving `"03000"`, and `=== 0` is false, so zero measured is judged non-zero. The counts are never checked as counts, only `bad` is. A report built by another path can pass with garbage states.
findings.fix: Require `AVAILABILITY_STATES.every(k => isCount(states[k]))` before summing, and refuse otherwise.
findings.twin_of: A fail-closed counter with open holes -> in a gate whose pass is 0, every unknown is not-zero
